value: Four stages on top of SmolLM3-3B: LoRA supervised fine-tuning on a synthetic formal-logic corpus; checkpoint fusion (parameter-space averaging of intermediate SFT checkpoints); WiSE-FT interpolation toward the base with λ = 0.25; and MGPO, entropy-weighted GRPO reinforcement learning against a programmatic verifier (published checkpoint step 2071).
quote: Four stages on top of the base model: [...] 1. **LoRA supervised fine-tuning** on a synthetic formal-logic corpus covering the Track A [...] 2. **Checkpoint fusion** — parameter-space averaging of intermediate SFT checkpoints selected [...] 3. **WiSE-FT interpolation** toward the pretrained base, `W = (1 − λ)·W_base + λ·W_finetuned` [...] 4. **MGPO** — entropy-weighted GRPO reinforcement learning against a programmatic verifier, with [...] Published checkpoint is **step 2071**.
quotes: Four stages on top of the base model:
1. **LoRA supervised fine-tuning** on a synthetic formal-logic corpus covering the Track A
2. **Checkpoint fusion** — parameter-space averaging of intermediate SFT checkpoints selected
3. **WiSE-FT interpolation** toward the pretrained base, `W = (1 − λ)·W_base + λ·W_finetuned`
4. **MGPO** — entropy-weighted GRPO reinforcement learning against a programmatic verifier, with
Published checkpoint is **step 2071**.

value: The card explains its training choices. WiSE-FT interpolation toward the base uses λ = 0.25, so only a quarter of the fine-tuned delta is kept. λ was chosen by constrained optimisation: maximise in-domain score subject to minimal degradation on held-out benchmarks. The card says this conservative λ is the direct reason held-out capability survives. Checkpoint fusion averages intermediate SFT checkpoints selected by a diversity probe, instead of taking the final checkpoint. MGPO (entropy-weighted GRPO) uses a programmatic verifier with partial credit for loose matches and token-F1, so that all-fail prompt groups still produce gradient. A sibling arm without the conservative interpolation scored higher in-domain but lost roughly twelve points of held-out capability, so this release is the balanced point of that trade.
quote:
**Checkpoint fusion** — parameter-space averaging of intermediate SFT checkpoints selected
   by a diversity probe, rather than taking the final checkpoint. [...] **WiSE-FT interpolation** toward the pretrained base, `W = (1 − λ)·W_base + λ·W_finetuned`
   with **λ = 0.25** — i.e. only a quarter of the fine-tuned delta is retained. λ was chosen by
   constrained optimisation: maximise in-domain score subject to minimal degradation on held-out
   benchmarks. This conservative λ is the direct reason held-out capability survives. [...] **MGPO** — entropy-weighted GRPO reinforcement learning against a programmatic verifier, with
   partial credit for loose matches and token-F1 so that all-fail prompt groups still produce
   gradient. [...] A sibling arm that skipped stage 3's conservative interpolation scores considerably higher
in-domain (macro gate 0.515) but gives back roughly twelve points of held-out capability. This
release is the balanced point of that trade; the other was not published.
quotes:
**Checkpoint fusion** — parameter-space averaging of intermediate SFT checkpoints selected
   by a diversity probe, rather than taking the final checkpoint.

**WiSE-FT interpolation** toward the pretrained base, `W = (1 − λ)·W_base + λ·W_finetuned`
   with **λ = 0.25** — i.e. only a quarter of the fine-tuned delta is retained. λ was chosen by
   constrained optimisation: maximise in-domain score subject to minimal degradation on held-out
   benchmarks. This conservative λ is the direct reason held-out capability survives.

**MGPO** — entropy-weighted GRPO reinforcement learning against a programmatic verifier, with
   partial credit for loose matches and token-F1 so that all-fail prompt groups still produce
   gradient.

A sibling arm that skipped stage 3's conservative interpolation scores considerably higher
in-domain (macro gate 0.515) but gives back roughly twelve points of held-out capability. This
release is the balanced point of that trade; the other was not published.

value: Limitations stated: 4.4% of Track A generations hit the 2048-token cap (above the 2% rankable threshold), so the Track A macro gate is indicative rather than exact. It is tuned for formal logic only, and code generation and tool use were not evaluated. It is not a chat model: it has no safety tuning beyond what the base carries, no instruction-following alignment work, and IFEval regressed slightly. A short generation budget truncates the <think> reasoning and scores far worse.

the base's 17.4%, but still above the 2% threshold our protocol requires to mark a comparison
`rankable`. The Track A macro gate should therefore be read as indicative rather than exact. [...] **Scope.** Tuned for formal logic. The Track B suite does not cover code generation or tool use
(HumanEval, LiveCodeBench and BFCL were not run for this model or its base), so this release
makes no claim about those. [...] **Not a chat model.** It was optimised against automatic verifiers on logic tasks. It has had no
safety tuning beyond whatever the base model carries, and no instruction-following alignment
